summary: Full-read extraction checkpoint for a cohomological circle method: Hankel-rank major arcs, Artin–Schreier cancellation, configuration-space E1 terms, monodromy parity, geometric Weyl differencing, function-field lattice shrinking, and a conditional comparison with double loop spaces. A rounding inequality and an odd-kd stratification error leave the sharp published-range proof unclosed; a conservative replacement range is derived below. Generic étale operations are imported, not replanned. No theorem is claimed formalised. Continuation: full published text read; the compact-open interpretation of the prescribed-germ space has a winding obstruction, even for a Fermat hypersurface in the main parameter range. Lemma7.2 requires a different, explicitly specified topology. Fixed-collar straightening is separated from the still-unproved comparison with that topology.

conventions.geometry: K a field; n≥2, k≥3; f∈K[x1,…,xn] has degree k, X={f=0} smooth affine, and its leading form f0 defines a smooth projective hypersurface Z⊂P^{n−1}. Fix a NONZERO vector x∈K^n with f0(x)=0, representing P∈Z. A chosen representative, not only the projective class, fixes the leading coefficients.
conventions.ranges: D=d(n−k), L=kd, K0=k−1, t=floor(d/K0), δ=n/2^k−k+1. Main range d≥K0≥2 and δ>0. Integer cohomological indices; thresholds are rational strict inequalities. Acyclic cohomological degree and dimension of an empty differencing locus are −∞, with extended arithmetic.
conventions.coefficients: Étale cohomology is geometric compact-support cohomology unless explicitly ordinary. In characteristic p assume p>k; choose ℓ≠p of even multiplicative order modulo p when using sign-conjugacy/minor arcs. Rank-one Artin–Schreier sheaves use E=Q_ℓ(μ_p); retain the coefficient-extension/descent debt before asserting all constructions over Q_ℓ. Frobenius convention gives E(−a) eigenvalue q^a. In characteristic zero spread out the full pair (f,x), not f alone.
conventions.derived: Cohomological shift: H^i(C[a])=H^{i+a}(C). Thus RΓ_c(A^r,E)=E[−2r](−r). Reduced compact cohomology means the homotopy fibre of the trace, not unreduced cohomology with an informal top-degree deletion. S_m acts with Koszul signs on derived tensor powers.
conventions.planning: All APIs, tests, modules, dependencies and proofs below are plans. No Lean file or Lean compilation is supplied. The corrected conservative range is a mathematical deduction from the paper's intermediate bounds, not an independently formalised proof. Original sharp claims are retained as explicitly gated targets, never silently certified.

items.name: Polynomial mapping scheme with a fixed leading vector
items.statement: Mor_{d,x} represents g_j=x_j T^d+Σ_{i<d}a_{i,j}T^i with f(g_1,…,g_n)=0. It is an affine scheme in nd coefficients cut out by the kd non-leading coefficients; f0(x)=0 kills degree kd. Individual g_j have degree ≤d; their joint degree is d. No quotient by reparametrization is taken.
unitTests: x_j=0 allows deg(g_j)<d
g↦g(aT+b) changes the fixed leading vector by a^d

items.name: Expected dimension lower bound
items.statement: Every nonempty irreducible component of Mor_{d,x} over an algebraic closure has dimension at least nd−kd=D, since there are kd defining equations.

items.name: Ordered and unordered configurations of the affine line
items.statement: PConf_m={ (a_1,…,a_m)∈A^m : a_i≠a_j for i≠j }; its S_m quotient is Conf_m, the open space of squarefree monic degree-m polynomials. The quotient map is a finite étale S_m-torsor, including m=0 as a point.
unitTests: PConf_0=Spec K, PConf_1=A1
char K dividing m! does not prevent the constant S_m torsor from being étale

items.name: Middle compact cohomology and parity-twisted tensors
items.statement: V=H_c^{n−1}(X,E); define W_m=(RΓ_c(PConf_m,E)⊗V^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}. The sign factor comes from placing each V in cohomological degree n−1.
unitTests: m=0 gives E in degree 0
transposition gives a minus sign exactly when n−1 is odd

items.name: Residue-coefficient phase
items.statement: For a∈A^{dn}, b∈A^L set e(a,b)=[T^{−1}](Σ_{r=1}^L b_rT^{−r})f(g_1(T),…,g_n(T)). This is a polynomial map A^{dn}×A^L→A1, linear in b and of degree ≤k in a.
unitTests: b=0 gives 0
adding a constant c to f changes e by c*b1

items.name: Artin–Schreier rank-one coefficient sheaf
items.statement: For nontrivial ψ:(F_p,+)→E× and E containing μ_p, L_ψ is the ψ-isotypical summand of the pushforward of E along u↦u^p−u. It is lisse rank one, additive under pullback, and L_ψ(−z)=L_{ψ^{-1}}(z).
unitTests: ψ=1 yields the constant sheaf, not an acyclic one
a nontrivial rank-one ψ need not exist over Q_ℓ itself

items.name: Geometric exponential-sum complex
items.statement: For p2:A^{dn}×A^L→A^L set S_{d,f}=Rp2! e*L_ψ. Its geometric stalk at b is RΓ_c(A^{dn},L_ψ(e(−,b))).
unitTests: b=0 stalk E[−2dn](−dn)
do not replace ! by ordinary pushforward

items.name: Cohomological Fourier orthogonality
items.statement: H_c^i(Mor_{d,x},E)≅H_c^{i+2kd}(A^{kd},S_{d,f})(kd), compatibly with Frobenius over F_q. Integrating the L linear phase variables gives zero off the coefficient-zero locus and E[−2L](−L) on it.

items.name: Hankel-rank geometric major arcs
items.statement: For 0≤m≤L, A_m^L⊂A^L is cut out by rank((b_{i+j−1})_{1≤i≤L−m,1≤j≤m+1})≤m. Set A_{−1}=∅ and A_m=A^L for m>L. Distinguish closed subschemes from their underlying reduced strata when using dimensions.
unitTests: m=0 gives b=0
L=9,m=4,b5=1 gives an invertible 5×5 matrix

items.name: Closedness and nesting of major arcs
items.statement: A_m^L is closed and A_m^L⊂A_{m+1}^L for every nonnegative m; A_0={0}.

items.name: Exact automatic-full range
items.statement: A_m^L=A^L for m≥ceil(L/2). For odd L the preceding A_floor(L/2)^L need not be full.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lem.2.4(3); corrected use p.38

items.name: Hankel rank and Padé approximation
items.statement: For m≤L and b∈A^L, b∈A_m iff there are 0≤m'≤m, monic h2 of degree m', and h1 of degree <m', such that Σ_{r≤L}b_rT^{−r}=h1/h2+O(T^{−L−1+m−m'}). Here O means all exponents at most the indicated exponent.

items.name: Unique reduced approximation on a rank stratum
items.statement: If 0≤m≤L/2 and b∈A_m\A_{m−1}, the triple (m',h1,h2) in padeexist is unique, h1,h2 are coprime, and if m'<m the coefficient at T^{−L−1+m−m'} in the error is nonzero.

items.name: Exact-denominator major-arc open
items.statement: For 0≤m≤L/2 define U_m^L⊂A_m\A_{m−1} by the existence of coprime h1,h2 with h2 monic of exact degree m and b=h1/h2+O(T^{−L−1}). This fixes all L Laurent coefficients.
unitTests: a lower-degree denominator belongs to the boundary, not U_m

items.name: Polynomial-pair model of the good arc
items.statement: U_m^L is open in A_m^L and isomorphic to {(h1,h2):deg h1<m, h2 monic degree m, gcd(h1,h2)=1}. In particular dim U_m=2m; the Padé rank-stratum description gives dim A_m≤2m when 2m≤L.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lem.3.1 pp.15–16; use p.38

items.name: Cancellation along a nontrivial additive orbit
items.statement: Let Y be a variety over a separably closed field of characteristic p, φ:Y→A1, u∈O(Y)×, and a:G_a×Y→Y an action with φ(a(λ,y))=φ(y)+u(y)λ. Then RΓ_c(Y,φ*L_ψ)=0. Prove u is orbit-invariant and normalize the orbit coordinate by u.

items.name: Lower-denominator boundary cancellation
items.statement: For 0≤m≤d the stalks of S_{d,f} vanish on (A_m^L\A_{m−1}^L)\U_m^L. Hence its compact cohomology on the stratum equals that on U_m.

items.name: Remainder fibration on the good arc
items.statement: For 0≤m≤d the polynomial remainder map ρ:A^{dn}×U_m→A^{mn}×U_m, g↦g mod h2, is an affine-space bundle of dimension n(d−m). The phase factors as e=ebar∘ρ.
unitTests: m=d gives relative dimension zero
m>d is excluded

items.name: Residue-class exponential complex
items.statement: Let p2':A^{mn}×U_m→U_m and π2:U_m→A^m, (h1,h2)↦h2. Set Sbar_{m,f}=Rπ2! Rp2'! ebar*L_ψ on the space of monic degree-m polynomials.
unitTests: Sbar_0=E
Rπ2! cannot be treated as a sheaf on U_m

items.name: Affine-fibre shift and twist
items.statement: Rρ!E=E[−2n(d−m)](−n(d−m)); H_c^i(U_m,S)=H_c^{i−2n(d−m)}(A^m,Sbar_m)(−n(d−m)) for m≤d.

items.name: Coprime multiplicativity
items.statement: Over pairs of coprime monic l1,l2 of degrees m1,m2, pullback of Sbar_{m1+m2} along multiplication is Sbar_{m1}⊠Sbar_{m2}. The isomorphism uses g modulo l1,l2 and h1=h11*l2+h12*l1; it is symmetric under swapping the two factors with the derived Koszul symmetry.

items.name: Nonsquarefree-modulus cancellation
items.statement: If X is smooth and h2 is monic nonsquarefree, the stalk of Sbar_m at h2 is zero. Reduce to h2=(T−a)^r, r≥2, and distinguish f(g(a))=0 (use a nonzero gradient) from f(g(a))≠0 (translate h1).

items.name: Reduced compact cohomology via trace fibre
items.statement: For smooth geometrically irreducible X of dimension n−1 define RΓ_c,red(X,E)=fib(RΓ_c(X,E)→E[−2(n−1)](−(n−1))). The map is the smooth trace and induces an isomorphism in top degree.
unitTests: X=A^{n−1} gives an acyclic fibre
non-geometrically-irreducible X needs a componentwise trace target

items.name: One-parameter exponential cohomology
items.statement: For the smooth X in the standing hypotheses, RΓ_c(G_m×A^n,L_ψ(h f(a)))≅RΓ_c,red(X,E)[−2](−1). The proof uses the zero locus in the G_a-parameter calculation and surjectivity of the relevant trace map.

items.name: Linear-modulus constant complex
items.statement: Sbar_{1,f} on A1 is the constant complex with value RΓ_c,red(X,E)[−2](−1). Translation of the unique root gives the canonical model.

items.name: Configuration-space descent for all moduli
items.statement: RΓ_c(A^m,Sbar_m)≅(RΓ_c(PConf_m,E)⊗RΓ_c,red(X,E)^{⊗m})^{S_m}[−2m](−m). Use repeated-modulus vanishing, CRT and the finite étale root-ordering torsor; invariants are exact over E.

items.name: Major-arc stratum complex
items.statement: For 0≤m≤d, RΓ_c(A_m\A_{m−1},S)≅(RΓ_c(PConf_m)⊗RΓ_c,red(X)^{⊗m})^{S_m}[−2m−2n(d−m)](−m−n(d−m)). The m≤d condition is essential.

items.name: Reduced cohomology concentrated in the middle
items.statement: Under smoothness of X and of its degree-k projective boundary, H_c,red^i(X,E)=0 for i≠n−1, and H_c,red^{n−1}=H_c^{n−1}. Use affine vanishing and weak Lefschetz on Xbar and Z.

items.name: Explicit cohomology of each major-arc stratum
items.statement: For 0≤m≤d, H_c^i(A_m\A_{m−1},S)≅(H_c^{i+m(n−1)−2nd}(PConf_m,E)⊗V^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}(−m−n(d−m)).

items.name: Universal smooth polynomial and boundary-point family
items.statement: M_{n,k} parametrizes (f,x) with f degree k, X and Z smooth, x≠0 and f0(x)=0. Let pr_{M,X}:𝓧→M be the universal affine hypersurface; h_n and h_{n−1} send (f,x) to the projective homogenization and leading-form hypersurfaces.
unitTests: rescaling f preserves X but changes the parameter point
projectivizing x forgets a G_m fibre

items.name: Primitive universal hypersurface local system
items.statement: For the parameter space H_{r,k} of smooth degree-k hypersurfaces in P^r, Prim_{r,k} is the primitive part of R^{r−1}π!E. In even cohomological degree split off the ambient hyperplane-class Tate line using its nonzero self-intersection.
unitTests: r=2 gives a symplectic H1
quadrics have primitive rank 0 or 1 depending on parity

items.name: Universal affine compact-cohomology support
items.statement: R^i pr_{M,X}!E vanishes except in degrees n−1 and 2(n−1), is lisse in those degrees, and R^{2(n−1)}=E(−(n−1)).
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lem.4.2 first assertions pp.27–28

items.name: Extension by boundary and projective primitives
items.statement: There is an exact sequence 0→h_{n−1}*Prim_{n−1,k}→R^{n−1}pr_{M,X}!E→h_n*Prim_{n,k}→0. Prove via localization and hyperplane classes, separately for the parity of n.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lem.4.2 final assertion pp.27–28

items.name: Full universal hypersurface monodromy
items.statement: For hypersurface dimension r−1≥1 and k≥3, excluding (r−1,k)=(2,3), Katz–Sarnak 11.4.9 gives geometric monodromy Sp on primitive middle cohomology for r−1 odd and the full O for r−1 even, over every geometric characteristic ≠ℓ. Degree-two primitives are handled directly. This is Zariski monodromy, not an E-point openness assertion.

items.name: Monodromy pullback along the universal pair maps
items.statement: For n≥3, h_n and h_{n−1} are smooth with geometrically connected generic fibres, and their normal targets give surjections on geometric étale fundamental groups. Include the scalar and nonzero-vector factors omitted from the informal description when constructing the maps.

items.name: Orthogonal–symplectic product criterion
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero coefficient field, a closed subgroup of O_a×Sp_b projecting onto both factors is the full product when a≥6 and the orthogonal and symplectic simple quotients have no exceptional isomorphism. Handle b=0 and disconnected O separately; use algebraic-group Goursat, not only abstract-group Goursat.

items.name: A monodromy element with only eigenvalue minus one
items.statement: For k≥2,n≥3,(k,n)≠(3,3),(3,4), geometric monodromy of R^{n−1}pr_{M,X}!E contains an element all of whose eigenvalues are −1. It need not be the scalar −Id on the nonsplit extension; generalized eigenspaces suffice.

items.name: Relative stratum formula and lissity
items.statement: For 0≤m≤d, R^i pr_{M,m}!S≅(H_c^{i+m(n−1)−2nd}(PConf_m,E)⊗(R^{n−1}pr_{M,X}!E)^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}(−m−n(d−m)); all these sheaves are lisse.

items.name: Odd-page differential vanishing in the verified parameter range
items.statement: For n≥3,k≥2,(k,n)≠(3,3),(3,4), the finite major-arc spectral sequence has d_r=0 for every odd r: a universal monodromy element has eigenvalue (−1)^m on column m and the opposite eigenvalue on column m+r. Restrict the standalone proposition to these hypotheses until its omitted exceptional cases are supplied; all main-theorem parameters satisfy them.

items.name: Finite closed-filtration spectral sequence with convergence
items.statement: For a bounded constructible complex F on Y filtered by finitely many closed Y_{−1}=∅⊂Y0⊂⋯⊂Yd=Y, construct E1^{m,s}=H_c^{m+s}(Y_m\Y_{m−1},F), d_r:(m,s)↦(m+r,s−r+1), and the exhaustive finite filtration on H_c^{m+s}(Y,F). Page/homology data alone do not prove convergence.

items.name: Major-arc first page before the global shift
items.statement: For 0≤m≤d, E1^{m,s}=(H_c^{s+mn−2nd}(PConf_m,E)⊗V^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}(−m−n(d−m)); outside this column range it is zero. It converges to H_c^{m+s}(A_d,S).

items.name: Finite-difference constancy locus with an explicit order
items.statement: For polynomial G:A^N→A1 and integer k≥1 with deg G≤k, let V_k(G)⊂(A^N)^{k−1} consist of tuples y for which Δ_{y1}⋯Δ_{y{k−1}}G(x) is independent of x. Define dd_k(G)=dim V_k(G), allowing −∞. The parameter k is part of the data even when deg G<k.
unitTests: k=1 and nonconstant affine G gives V empty
if deg G<k then V is the whole parameter space

items.name: Exponential compact-cohomological degree
items.statement: cd_ψ(G)=sup{i∈Z:H_c^i(A^N,L_ψ(G))≠0}, with value −∞ for an acyclic complex. The value is unchanged by coefficient-field extension and polynomial coordinate isomorphisms.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Def.5.2 p.32 and proof of Prop.5.5
unitTests: constant phase has cd=2N
nonconstant affine-linear phase has cd=−∞

items.name: Sign reversal by coefficient conjugation
items.statement: If ℓ has even order modulo p, cd_ψ(G)=cd_ψ(−G). A power of the unramified coefficient-field Frobenius on Q_ℓ(μ_p) sends μ_p to its inverse, giving semilinear cohomology isomorphisms.

items.name: Tensor-product and difference identities for cohomological degree
items.statement: cd(G)+cd(−G)=cd(G(x)−G(y))=cd(G(x)−G(x+y)); use the compact-support Künneth formula and an invertible triangular coordinate change. Interpret all identities in Z∪{−∞}.

items.name: Geometric Weyl-differencing bound
items.statement: For G in N variables of degree ≤k over F_q, p>k and ℓ of even order modulo p, cd(G)≤[dd_k(G)+N(2^{k−1}−(k−1))]/2^{k−2}. Include k=1 and all acyclic fibres; prove by differencing, projection, support dimension and induction.

items.name: Top-degree multilinear polarization
items.statement: In p>k write G_k(x)=Σ c_{i1,…,ik}x_i1⋯x_ik with symmetric c. The coefficients of x in the (k−1)-fold difference are k! times the corresponding symmetric multilinear forms. Thus V_k(G)=V_k(G_k) is cut out by N multilinear equations.
unitTests: p dividing k! is excluded
adding lower-degree terms does not change V_k

items.name: All-extension point bounds detect dimension
items.statement: Let V be finite type over F_q. If one constant C satisfies #V(F_{q^r})≤C q^{rD} for every r≥1, then dim V≤D. Apply Lang–Weil on an irreducible component after its finite field of definition; a bound only over F_q is insufficient.

items.name: Lang–Weil lower asymptotic needed by differencing
items.statement: For geometrically irreducible finite-type V/F_Q of dimension e, #V(F_{Q^r})=Q^{re}+O_V(Q^{r(e−1/2)}) as r→∞ (with the zero-dimensional case separate). An irreducible geometric component descends to a finite extension. Only this input, not smooth-projective RH alone, proves extensiondimension.

items.name: Differencing-dimension bound outside a rank arc
items.statement: For d≥k−1, d≤m≤kd/2 and b∉A_m^{kd}, the degree-≤k polynomial G_b(a)=e(a,b) in dn variables satisfies dd_k(G_b)≤dn(k−1)−n floor(m/(k−1)), assuming smooth f0 and p>k.

items.name: Stalk cohomology supported on a major arc
items.statement: Under the same range and the even-order coefficient-prime hypothesis, the cohomology sheaf H^i(S_{d,f}) is supported on A_m whenever i>n(2d−floor(m/(k−1))/2^{k−2}).

items.name: Correct finite stratification of the minor arcs
items.statement: A^L\A_d=⊔_{m=d}^{ceil(L/2)−1}(A_{m+1}\A_m). The top index is a ceiling minus one; replacing it by floor(L/2)−1 misses the last stratum when L is odd.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Proof of Prop.2.6 p.38, corrected

items.name: Conservative minor-arc vanishing with rounding retained
items.statement: Under the main hypotheses, H_c^j(A^L\A_d,S)=0 for j>2dn+4(k−1)−4tδ. Indeed each stratum has upper cohomological bound B(m)=2dn−n floor(m/(k−1))/2^{k−2}+4(m+1); writing m=(k−1)q+r yields B(m)=2dn−4qδ+4(r+1)≤2dn−4tδ+4(k−1). This is the proved arithmetic correction to the displayed method, conditional on its geometric intermediate inputs.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Prop.2.6 and proof p.38, conservative repair

items.name: Unclosed sharp minor-arc target
items.statement: Target stated in Prop.2.6: under the main hypotheses, H_c^j(A^L\A_d,S)=0 for j>2dn+4−4tδ. The proof printed on p.38 does not establish it. No unconditional certification is made: a new estimate improving the rounding remainder is required. Use minorsafe until that input exists.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Prop.2.6 p.12; proof p.38

items.name: Shifted finite-field E1 formula
items.statement: Shift the major-arc complex by 2dn and twist by kd. For 0≤m≤d, E1^{m,s}=(H_c^{s+mn}(PConf_m,E)⊗V^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}(kd−m−n(d−m)), zero otherwise; d_r has bidegree (r,1−r) and odd r vanish in the main range.

items.name: Conservative cohomology comparison range
items.statement: The shifted major-arc spectral sequence converges to a complex whose degree-i cohomology is H_c^{i+2D}(Mor_{d,x},E), Frobenius-equivariantly over F_q, for i>−4(tδ−(k−1)). Use minorsafe, the localization triangle, and orthogonality. Over general K it is a noncanonical vector-space comparison after spreading out the full pair.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Thm.2.7(3); Thm.1.1, conservative repaired range

items.name: Original sharp comparison target, explicitly gated
items.statement: Theorems 1.1 and 2.7 claim the preceding comparison for i>−4(tδ−1). Retain that exact target only as conditional on minorsharpgate and coefficient descent/spreading closure; it is not established by this checkpoint.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Thm.1.1 p.2; Thm.2.7(3) p.12

items.name: Spreading out the pair and cohomology
items.statement: Choose a finitely generated subring R⊂K containing coefficients of f AND coordinates x, invert suitable elements for x≠0, degrees and both smoothness conditions, and stratify compact-cohomology pushforwards to obtain a common lisse open for finitely many nonzero degrees. Transport ranks to a closed finite-field point; in characteristic zero also choose p>k with ℓ of even order mod p.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Proof of Thm.1.1 p.13
unitTests: x need not lie in the ring generated by f's coefficients
Spec K need not equal Spec Frac R

items.name: Configuration compact-cohomology support
items.statement: For m≥1, H_c^a(PConf_m,E)=0 unless m+1≤a≤2m. Translation gives PConf_m≅A1×(PConf_m/G_a), with the quotient affine smooth of dimension m−1; use affine vanishing, duality and the A1 shift. For m=0 only a=0 survives.

items.name: E1 support region
items.statement: E1^{m,s} can be nonzero only at (m,s)=(0,0), or 1≤m≤d with −m(n−1)+1≤s≤−m(n−2).

items.name: Compact cohomology vanishing bands
items.statement: Within the conservative comparison range i>−4(tδ−(k−1)), H_c^{i+2D}(Mor)=0 unless i=0 or 1−m(n−2)≤i≤−m(n−3) for some 1≤m≤d. The original Cor.1.2 asserts this in the sharper gated range.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Cor.1.2 p.3, repaired range

items.name: Automatic E1 degeneration near the top
items.statement: For m+s>1−2(n−2)(n−3), E∞^{m,s}=E1^{m,s}. A potentially nonzero r≥2 differential forces m≥r(n−3)+2≥2n−4. To identify these terms with Mor cohomology also impose the applicable comparison range.

items.name: Conservative irreducibility and expected dimension
items.statement: If d≥k−1≥2, p=0 or p>k, and tδ>k−1, then the corrected comparison reaches i=0; Mor_{d,x} is geometrically irreducible of dimension D. Combine top compact cohomology of rank one with the componentwise dimension lower bound. The source's weaker endpoint condition tδ≥1 is not certified.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Cor.1.4/2.9 pp.6,14, conservative sufficient hypothesis

items.name: Small-degree excess-dimension example
items.statement: For 1≤d<k−1, f=x1^{k−1}x2+x2^k+⋯+xn^k+1, P=(1:0:⋯:0), p=0 or p>k, the x2=0 mapping locus has dimension at least D−d+k−1>D over an algebraically closed field. It is nonempty by a constant solution in the remaining coordinates.

items.name: Unproved E1-degeneration proposition
items.statement: Define, do not assert, the proposition that H_c^{i+2D}(Mor,E)≅⊕_{m≥0}(H_c^{i+m(n−1)}(PConf_m,E)⊗V^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m} for i>−4(tδ−1), under the main geometric and characteristic hypotheses. Terms beyond m=d vanish in the stated stable range. This is Conjecture1.3, not a theorem.
unitTests: odd-page vanishing alone does not imply d2=0

items.name: Function-field norm and fractional part
items.statement: On F_q((T^{−1})), |Σ_{i≤r}c_iT^i|=q^r for c_r≠0, |0|=0. The fractional part keeps negative powers; ||α|| is its norm. Vector norms are maxima. Strict |u|<q^h for u∈F_q[T] means deg u<h.
unitTests: |T|=q while the formal-series variable X=T^{-1} has norm q^{-1}

items.name: Polar forms of the leading hypersurface
items.statement: For symmetric coefficients c of f0, set Ψ_j(u^(1),…,u^(k−1))=k!Σ_{j1,…,j{k−1}}c_{j1,…,j{k−1},j}∏_r u_{j_r}^{(r)}. On the diagonal Ψ_j(u,…,u)=(k−1)!∂_j f0(u).
unitTests: p>k makes the factorial invertible
smooth Z makes the common diagonal zero locus {0}

items.name: Degree-k part of the residue phase
items.statement: The degree-k homogeneous part of G_b(a) equals Σ_{j1,…,jk}Σ_{0≤i1,…,ik<d}c_{j1,…,jk} b_{i1+⋯+ik+1}∏_r a_{i_r,j_r}. The full G_b may have lower-degree terms, but V_k(G_b)=V_k((G_b)_k).
items.locator: arXiv v3, §6 pp.38–39, corrected full-polynomial identity

items.name: Function-field differencing count
items.statement: N(α)=#{u=(u^(1),…,u^(k−1))∈F_q[T]^{n(k−1)}: |u^(r)|<q^d and ||α Ψ_j(u)||<q^{−d} for all j}. For 0≤s≤d define N_s by replacing the box q^d by q^{d−s} and the fractional threshold q^{−d} by q^{−d−(k−1)s}.
unitTests: N_s≥1 from the zero tuple
strict thresholds include neither degree boundary

items.name: Differencing points equal the arithmetic count
items.statement: For α=Σ_{r=1}^{kd}b_rT^{−r}, #V_k(G_b)(F_q)=N(α). Matching coefficients turns each polarization equation into the vanishing of the first d negative coefficients of αΨ_j.

items.name: Uniform minor-arc differencing count
items.statement: For d≥k−1, d≤m≤kd/2 and b∉A_m^{kd}, N(α)≪_{d,k,n}q^{dn(k−1)−n floor(m/(k−1))}. The implied constant is independent of q and of extension degree; p>k and smoothness of f0 are required.

items.name: Polynomial lattices over the Laurent local field
items.statement: For invertible M∈GL_N(F_q((T^{-1}))), the lattice is M F_q[T]^N. Its adjoint is (M^{-1})^t F_q[T]^N relative to the standard dot pairing. Define successive minima R_i as the least radii with i independent lattice vectors; keep strict/open-ball counting conventions distinct.
unitTests: rank one T^a F_q[T] has first minimum q^a
replacing M by a singular matrix is invalid

items.name: Ultrametric reduced basis and exact box count
items.statement: A full polynomial lattice has a norm-orthogonal reduced basis with norms R_i. Its number of vectors of norm <q^h is ∏_i max(q^h/R_i,1) when h is integral. The product formula uses the discrete value group and polynomial coefficient counts.

items.name: Adjoint successive-minima duality
items.statement: For a lattice Λ and its adjoint Λ*, ordered minima satisfy R_i(Λ)R_{N+1−i}(Λ*)=1. Prove the nonarchimedean reduced-basis theorem rather than importing Euclidean Minkowski bounds.

items.name: Symmetric simultaneous-approximation counting function
items.statement: For symmetric γ∈M_n(F_q((T^{-1}))) and integers a,c with c>0, N_{γ,a,c}=#{u∈F_q[T]^n: |u|<q^a, ||γu||<q^{−c}}. The auxiliary polynomial vector eliminating the integer part is unique because c>0.
unitTests: γ=0 gives q^{n max(a,0)}
a≤0 leaves only u=0

items.name: Duality for the symmetric block lattice
items.statement: For Λ represented by [[T^{−a}I,0],[T^cγ,T^c I]], γ symmetric, the adjoint is isometric to T^{a−c}Λ after sign changes and swapping blocks. Hence R_iR_{2n+1−i}=q^{c−a}.

items.name: Exact symmetric-lattice shrinking inequality
items.statement: For a,c,s∈Z, c>0,s≥0 and γ symmetric, N_{γ,a,c}/N_{γ,a−s,c+s}≤q^{ns+n max(floor((a−c)/2),0)}. Equivalently clear the positive denominator. Derive by separating minima pairs across the unit radius.

items.name: Iterated multilinear shrinking
items.statement: In the setting of Nalpha, for integer 0≤s≤d, N(α)≤q^{(k−1)ns}N_s(α). Shrink one vector block at a time; polarization symmetry makes each coefficient matrix symmetric and the floor correction zero.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Proof of Prop.6.2 p.42

items.name: Minor-arc exclusion forces the shrunken polar values to vanish
items.statement: Take s=d−floor(m/(k−1)). If b∉A_m and u is counted by N_s, then every Ψ_j(u)=0. A nonzero Ψ_j would give a rational approximation to α with denominator degree at most m and the error required by Lem.2.4, contradicting b∉A_m.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Proof of Prop.6.2 pp.42–43

items.name: Dimension bound for the common polar-zero variety
items.statement: For smooth f0 and p>k, W={Ψ_1=⋯=Ψ_n=0}⊂A^{n(k−1)} has dim W≤n(k−2): its intersection with the diagonal A^n is only 0, and the affine dimension inequality gives the bound.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Proof of Prop.6.2 p.43

items.name: Degree-uniform polynomial point bound
items.statement: For affine V⊂A^N over F_q(T), defined over F_q[T], of dimension e and degree Δ, the number of polynomial points with |u|<q^h is O_{Δ,N}(q^{he}) for integral h≥1, uniformly in q. The application is to W of bounded degree depending only on n,k; dimension zero and h=0 need separate elementary handling.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Proof of Prop.6.2 citing [4] Lem.2.8; original author PDF p.12

items.name: Continuous mapping space with prescribed infinity germ
items.statement: For K=C define Hom_{d,P} using continuous maps P1(C)→Xbar, sending ∞ to P, finite points into X, and with local homogeneous coordinates (x1+O(|z|),…,xn+O(|z|),z^d+O(|z|^{d+1})) near z=0. A formal construction must specify the topology and uniformity of germ bounds in families before claiming homotopy equivalences.
unitTests: a family of shrinking neighbourhoods is not automatically a uniform homotopy
not the full unrestricted continuous mapping space
The escapingloop example prevents using an unspecified compact-open Hom≃Ω²X equivalence.
items.note: Source leaves topology unspecified. See compacthom for the explicit compact-open interpretation and compactcounter for its obstruction.

items.name: Unproved algebraic-to-continuous trace comparison
items.statement: For X as above over C define the assertion that the cup-product/trace pairing H_c^{2D−j}(Mor,Q)⊗H^j(Hom_{d,P},Q)→Q is perfect for 0≤j<4(tδ−1). This is Conjecture7.1. It is not a claim that Mor is smooth or proper, nor a proved comparison theorem.
unitTests: a conjecture is not registered as an instance or axiom
finite-dimensional duality requires the range and irreducibility inputs
The escapingloop example prevents using an unspecified compact-open Hom≃Ω²X equivalence.
items.note: The topology is material: no corrected stronger-topology version is silently substituted into the source conjecture.

items.name: Continuous mapping space versus the double loop space
items.statement: When Hom_{d,P} is nonempty, Lem.7.2 claims a homotopy equivalence Hom_{d,P}≃Ω²X. Fix a reference map with the same infinity germ, straighten the germ and glue two discs. Supply uniform-family continuity and the chosen mapping-space topology; this checkpoint has not closed that construction. For the compact-open topology this assertion is false by compactcounter; any corrected endpoint must specify a stronger topology and discharge stronggermgate.

items.name: Signed Witt–Euler exponents
items.statement: For N≥0 and a fixed parity n, define integers e_r(N) by ∏_{r≥1}(1−T^r)^{−e_r(N)}=1+(−1)^{n−1}NT in Z[[T]]. Coefficients are defined degreewise using only finitely many factors.
unitTests: N=0 gives every e_r=0
n odd,N=1 gives e1=1,e2=−1,e_r=0 for r>2

items.name: Möbius formula for the Euler exponents
items.statement: For r≥1, e_r(N)=−(1/r)Σ_{a|r}μ(a)((−1)^n N)^{r/a}. Use a formal logarithmic derivative and Möbius inversion; show integrality via the defining integer Euler product rather than division in Z without a proof.

items.name: Twisted configuration trace formula
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero S_m character χ, Σ_{f monic squarefree,deg f=m}χ(Frob_f)=Σ_a(−1)^a q^{m−a}〈χ,H^a(PConf_m,E)〉=Σ_i(−1)^{m−i}q^i〈χ,H_c^{m+i}(PConf_m,E)〉. The first cohomology is ORDINARY, not compactly supported.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lem.7.4 proof p.45; [6] Thm.3.7

items.name: Split hyperplane-complement cohomology
items.statement: For a finite set of hyperplanes defined over F_q in A^m and ℓ≠p, ordinary étale cohomology of their complement is generated by the degree-one hyperplane classes; H^a is a direct sum of E(−a), so Frobenius acts by q^a. Apply to PConf_m and compare with complex cohomology.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lem.7.4 input [6] Prop.3.3 and Thm.3.7

items.name: Twisted configuration multiplicities by Euler products
items.statement: For V of dimension N, dim(H_c^{m+i}(PConf_m,E)⊗V^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}=(−1)^{mn+i}[q^i U^m]∏_{r≥1}(1−qU^r)^{−e_r(N)}. The character of V^{⊗m} is N^{number of cycles}; the sign twist changes it by (−1)^{(n−1)(m−cycles)}.

items.name: Stable diagonal coefficient identity
items.statement: For integers j,d,N≥0,n>3 and d(n−3)≥j, Σ_{m=0}^d dim(H_c^{mn−m−j}(PConf_m,E)⊗V^{⊗m}⊗sgn^{n−1})^{S_m}=[q^{−j}]∏_{r≥1}(1−(−q)^{1−r(n−2)})^{−e_r(N)}. Extract the relevant weighted diagonal of the two-variable series; it is not the entire series.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Cor.7.5 p.46, corrected coefficient-extraction proof

items.name: Tame polynomial at infinity
items.statement: For a complex polynomial f, use Broughton's gradient criterion: outside a compact subset of C^n the gradient norm is bounded below by a positive constant. A smooth homogeneous leading form implies the stronger growth ||∇f(z)||≥c||z||^{k−1} for sufficiently large ||z|| by compactness of the unit sphere.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lem.7.6 proof p.46 citing [3]
unitTests: nonisolated leading-gradient zeros prevent this argument
the noncompact fibre need not be projective

items.name: Smooth tame fibre has the homotopy type of a sphere bouquet
items.statement: For a regular fibre X of a tame complex polynomial in n variables, the source uses Broughton Theorem2 to conclude X≃∨_N S^{n−1}, where N=dim H^{n−1}(X,Q). Exact original-source hypotheses and proof remain to be verified; retain this as an explicit prerequisite gate.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lem.7.6 proof p.46; [3] Thm.2

items.name: Hilton decomposition for an equal-dimensional wedge
items.statement: For n≥3, π_i(∨_N S^{n−1}) decomposes into the finite-degree relevant factors π_i(S^{w(n−2)+1}), with multiplicity (1/w)Σ_{a|w}μ(a)N^{w/a}. The original [14] Cor.4.10 and its wedge/product conventions require verification before implementation.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lem.7.6 proof pp.46–47; [14] Cor.4.10

items.name: Rational homotopy of simply connected spheres
items.statement: For m≥2, π_i(S^m)⊗Q has rank 1 at i=m, and also at i=2m−1 if m is even, and is zero otherwise. Do not extend the statement blindly to S1 and nonconnected iterated loops.

items.name: Rational homotopy ranks in signed Euler notation
items.statement: For n≥3 and X≃∨_N S^{n−1}, dim_Q π_{r(n−2)+1}(X)⊗Q=(−1)^{r(n−2)−1}e_r(N); all other positive rational homotopy groups vanish. For odd n, include the second rational homotopy class of even spheres in the Möbius calculation.

items.name: Rational cohomology of the connected double-loop H-space
items.statement: For n≥4 and X≃∨_N S^{n−1}, Ω²X is connected and of finite rational type degreewise. Its rational cohomology is a free graded-commutative algebra on the dual rational homotopy generators shifted down two degrees, with ranks given by wedgehomotopy. Verify Sullivan p.311's hypotheses before treating this as closed.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lem.7.6 proof p.47; [25] p.311

items.name: Double-loop Betti series in the connected range
items.statement: For n≥4 and smooth affine X⊂C^n with smooth degree-k leading form, dim H^j(Ω²X,Q)=[q^{−j}]∏_{r≥1}(1−(−q)^{1−r(n−2)})^{−e_r(N)}, where N=dim H^{n−1}(X,Q). This corrects the printed n≥2: at n=3 the full Ω²X can have infinitely many components. The coefficientwise product is well-defined for n≥4.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lem.7.6 pp.46–47, corrected range

items.name: Conditional implication from the comparison conjecture
items.statement: Over C in the main parameter range, Conjecture7.1 implies Conjecture1.3 PROVIDED the sharp spectral-sequence comparison, the mapping-space equivalence and the rational-homotopy prerequisites are established. Compare dimensions of H_c^{i+2D}(Mor), not ordinary cohomology, with the E1 diagonal via configdiagonal and loopbetti; dimensions force all differentials touching that diagonal to vanish.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Thm.7.7 pp.47–48, dependencies exposed

items.name: Shared constructible compact-support operations
items.statement: Use the single bounded constructible ℓ-adic category with Rf!, geometric stalk base change, localization triangles, projection formula, Künneth and coefficient extension. Verify separation/finite type and finite cohomological dimension in each application; no arbitrary six-functor-valued assumptions.
unitTests: open–closed exact sequence has the correct arrow direction

items.name: Smooth trace and duality
items.statement: For smooth pure r-dimensional Y over a separably closed field, RΓ_c(Y,E)⊗RΓ(Y,E)→E[−2r](−r) is the Poincaré pairing. For geometrically connected Y, H_c^{2r}=E(−r). Retain the negative Tate twist.

items.name: Weak Lefschetz for the projective closure and boundary
items.statement: For a smooth ample divisor Z in a smooth projective r-fold Xbar, H^i(Xbar,E)→H^i(Z,E) is an isomorphism for i<r−1 and injective for i=r−1; combine with the dual Gysin map and affine Artin vanishing.

items.name: Étale–singular comparison with compact supports
items.statement: For complex finite-type separated varieties and admissible coefficients, compare geometric étale and singular cohomology with compact supports, compatibly with traces, products and finite-group actions. Do not replace H_c by H in the nonproper mapping scheme.

items.name: Constructibility and smooth/proper base change
items.statement: Finite-type compact-support pushforwards are constructible with finite amplitude in the stated coefficient setting; smooth proper higher pushforwards are lisse. For nonproper morphisms use constructibility and an explicitly selected stratum, not global smooth-proper base change.

items.name: Shared singular and relative topology infrastructure
items.statement: Import relative singular chains, cohomology products, excision and manifold duality from the existing Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology roadmap; mapping spaces and rational homotopy add only the missing interfaces.
unitTests: homotopy-equivalent noncompact spaces need not have isomorphic compact-support cohomology

items.name: Additive character carrier
items.statement: AddChar A M stores a map from an additive monoid A to a multiplicative monoid M with ψ(0)=1 and ψ(a+b)=ψ(a)ψ(b).
unitTests: the trivial character is constant one
items.note: Declaration statement opened at the pinned commit; only the stated carrier/lemma is credited, not the paper-level theorem.

items.name: Finite character orthogonality
items.statement: For a finite additive group A and a domain commutative semiring R, the sum of ψ:AddChar A R is |A| for the trivial character and zero otherwise.
items.note: Declaration statement opened at the pinned commit; only the stated carrier/lemma is credited, not the paper-level theorem.

items.name: Laurent-series carrier
items.statement: LaurentSeries R is HahnSeries Z R. Use its formal variable as T^{-1}; this carrier alone is not the q-adic norm, polynomial lattice or fractional-part counting API.
unitTests: T corresponds to the inverse of the formal series variable
items.note: Declaration statement opened at the pinned commit; only the stated carrier/lemma is credited, not the paper-level theorem.

items.name: Cohomological spectral-sequence carrier
items.statement: CategoryTheory.CohomologicalSpectralSequence is SpectralSequence with complex-shape differential (r,1−r), including successive-page homology isomorphisms. It does not include the finite-filtration construction or convergence theorem.
unitTests: a sequence of pages is not an abutment filtration
items.note: Declaration statement opened at the pinned commit; only the stated carrier/lemma is credited, not the paper-level theorem.

items.name: Abstract group Goursat ingredient
items.statement: A subgroup of G×H projecting surjectively to both factors is described by a graph between quotient groups as in Subgroup.goursat_surjective. This is only the abstract group ingredient; closed algebraic-group quotients and Lie-type exclusions remain missing.
items.note: Declaration statement opened at the pinned commit; only the stated carrier/lemma is credited, not the paper-level theorem.

items.name: Generalized based loop carrier
items.statement: GenLoop is the subtype of continuous maps I^N→X sending Cube.boundary N to the basepoint. Taking N=Fin 2 supplies a double-loop carrier, not the paper's germ mapping-space equivalence.
unitTests: N=Fin 2 has an entire square boundary fixed
items.note: Declaration statement opened at the pinned commit; only the stated carrier/lemma is credited, not the paper-level theorem.

items.name: Iterated-loop homotopy shifts
items.statement: Tau Ceti supplies zerothHomotopyEquiv identifying components of generalized loops with the corresponding homotopy group, and piLoopSpaceMulEquiv shifting positive homotopy groups of iterated loops. These do not supply rational sphere or bouquet calculations.
items.note: Declaration statement opened at the pinned commit; only the stated carrier/lemma is credited, not the paper-level theorem.

items.name: Ring-valued divisor Möbius inversion
items.statement: For functions f,g:N→R with R a nonassociative ring, the identities Σ_{i|n} f(i)=g(n) for n>0 are equivalent to Σ_{(a,b):ab=n}μ(a)g(b)=f(n).
items.note: Declaration statement opened at the pinned commit; only the stated carrier/lemma is credited, not the paper-level theorem.

items.name: One-dimensional Fourier–Deligne transform
items.statement: For K∈D_c^b(A1,E), define FT_ψ(K)=Rpr2!(pr1*K⊗L_ψ(xy))[1]. Establish inversion, shifts, and the middle-extension behaviour needed below; this is not the finite numerical Fourier transform.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lem.3.7 p.23, author [16] §8.2.5(2), journal [15]
unitTests: constant sheaf transforms to a point-supported object with the prescribed shift

items.name: Fourier input for the one-modulus trace map
items.statement: For a nonconstant one-variable polynomial f of degree <p, the exponential family on G_m has the cohomological support used in Lem.3.7: RΓ_c(G_m×A1,L_ψ(hf(a))) is concentrated in degrees ≤2. The cited Fourier middle-extension/no-constant-quotient argument must be checked against Katz §8.2.5(2), with all exclusions explicit.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lem.3.7 p.23 citing Katz [16]; journal [15]

items.name: Affine étale cohomological dimension
items.statement: For an affine variety of dimension r over a separably closed field and a constructible torsion sheaf of order invertible in the field, H^i=0 for i>r; pass to the admissible ℓ-adic setting and use duality for lisse compact-support bounds. For arbitrary constructible compact supports use the 2r upper bound, not the affine r bound.
items.locator: Lem.2.8; Lem.3.11; Prop.5.5; SGA4 XIV Cor.3.2
items.note: EDC.4 explicitly imports the affine Artin-vanishing supplier; SF.2 is the shared scheme-cohomology interface.

items.name: Compact-open continuity from joint continuity
items.statement: For topological X,Y,Z and f:X→C(Y,Z), continuity of its uncurried evaluation implies continuity of f.

items.name: Joint evaluation for compact-open mapping spaces
items.statement: If Y is locally compact, evaluation C(Y,Z)×Y→Z is continuous, hence a continuous parameter map into C(Y,Z) uncurries continuously.
items.locator: Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean:245,455; instance and lemma statements freshly read at 082e2d3

items.name: Circle fundamental group and integer monodromy
items.statement: UnitAddCircle.fundamentalGroupMulEquiv identifies π1(R/Z,0) with Multiplicative Z; its apply_eq_iff characterizes the integer by the endpoint of the lift beginning at0. Circle.fundamentalGroupMulEquiv gives the corresponding group isomorphism for every basepoint of the complex unit circle.

items.name: CW cofibrations and cellular approximation suppliers
items.statement: Import CW cofibration, quotient-by-contractible-subcomplex and cellular-approximation arguments from upstream AlgebraicTopology Stages4 and8. They supply the finite-join calculation and the disk-boundary homotopy extension argument; these generic theorems are not replanned in the application.
items.locator: Freshly read upstream stages4,8; no matching reviewed audit entry for these upstream stages

items.name: Compact-open prescribed-germ mapping space
items.statement: Let Xbar be the smooth projective closure, X its affine chart, P its prescribed boundary point and d≥1. Hco is the subset of C(P1(C),Xbar) satisfying the pointwise conditions (7.1), with the subspace compact-open topology. The big-O constants and neighbourhood may depend on the map. This is one explicit interpretation of the source, not a claim about an unstated intended topology.
items.locator: Continuation, report topology analysis; journal pp.940–941
api: family_of_joint : joint continuous family with individual germs → continuous map to Hco; no uniform-germ conclusion
unitTests: Every F∈Hco has F(∞)=P.
A continuous map equal to a valid polynomial reference outside a compact subset of C lies in Hco.
The escapingloop family is Hco-continuous although its normalized normal germs fail to converge uniformly in the loop parameter.

tests.name: compacthom_exact_tail
tests.statement: A continuous map equal to a valid polynomial reference outside a compact subset of C lies in Hco.

tests.name: compacthom_escaping_phase
tests.statement: The escapingloop family is Hco-continuous although its normalized normal germs fail to converge uniformly in the loop parameter.

items.name: Shrinking degree-one phase loop
items.statement: For 0<r≤1/4 and s∈[0,1], put h(s,r)=max(0,min(1,(s−r)/r)) and σ(s,r)=exp(2πi h(s,r)). Descend in s through 0∼1. The lift h is retained for the integer monodromy computation.
items.locator: Continuation, report topology analysis; journal pp.940–941
api: sigma_degree : fixed r loop has degree1; eventual_one : fixed s, eventually r→0, σ=1
unitTests: sup_s |σ(s,r)−1|=2 for every permitted r.

items.name: Pointwise eventual constancy does not imply uniform germ control
items.statement: σ is jointly continuous for r>0; for every fixed s it is1 for all sufficiently small r, while each fixed-r loop has degree1. For s>0 take r<s/2; for s=0 use h=0. Its lifted endpoint difference is1, and s=3r/2 prevents uniform convergence.
items.locator: Continuation, report topology analysis; journal pp.940–941

items.name: Fermat hypersurface and polynomial reference map
items.statement: For k≥3,n≥3,d≥1 choose ζ∈C with ζ^k=−1. Let X={Σ_{j=1}^n x_j^k=1}, Xbar={Σ x_j^k=x0^k}, P=[1:ζ:0:…:0:0] and g(T)=(T^d,ζT^d,1,0,…). X, Xbar and Xbar∩{x0=0} are smooth, and g has the prescribed leading vector and germ.
items.locator: Continuation, report topology analysis; journal pp.940–941
api: fermat_pair(k,n) : smooth affine/projective pair; smooth_by_gradient : simultaneous gradient zero forces all homogeneous coordinates zero
reference(d,ζ) : C→X polynomial; reference_extension : P1→Xbar continuous
unitTests: g(0)=(0,0,1,0,…), so the affine map is defined at T=0.
k=3,d=2,n=40 gives d=k−1, n>2^k(k−1), δ=3 and t=1.

tests.name: fermatreference_zero
tests.statement: g(0)=(0,0,1,0,…), so the affine map is defined at T=0.

tests.name: fermatreference_main_range
tests.statement: k=3,d=2,n=40 gives d=k−1, n>2^k(k−1), δ=3 and t=1.

items.name: Continuous loop with an escaping phase transition
items.statement: For the Fermat pair let r(T)=1/(4(1+|T|)), a_s(T)=T^d σ(s,r(T)), and F_s(T)=(a_s(T),ζa_s(T),1,0,…), extended at∞ by P. This is a based continuous loop S1→Hco at g. For each fixed s its tail equals g exactly. Joint projective continuity at∞ follows from |a_s(T)|=|T|^d uniformly in s.
items.locator: Continuation, report topology analysis; journal pp.940–941
api: escaping_family : S1×P1→Xbar continuous; escaping_loop : Path g g in Hco
unitTests: Σ_j(F_s(T)_j)^k=1 for every finite T.
At s=3r(T)/2 the normalized normal coordinate (x0/x1)/T^(−d) is−1, however large positive T is.

tests.name: escapingloop_normal_control
tests.statement: At s=3r(T)/2 the normalized normal coordinate (x0/x1)/T^(−d) is−1, however large positive T is.

items.name: A compact parameter family has a common projective chart at infinity
items.statement: For compact K and continuous H:K→Hco, there is R0 such that H(u,T) lies in {x1≠0} for all u∈K and |T|>R0, assuming P has x1≠0. Joint evaluation and a finite subcover of K×{∞} give a common neighbourhood of∞. The normal coordinate v=x0/x1 is nonzero there for finite T because H(u,T)∈X. This does not assert uniform convergence of v/z^d.
items.locator: Continuation, report topology analysis; journal pp.940–941

items.name: Winding of a mapping-space loop at infinity
items.statement: For a based loop γ:S1→Hco in the Fermat example, choose any sufficiently large positive R and take the degree of the circle-valued normalization of γ(s)(R).x0/γ(s)(R).x1, divided by its value at the loop basepoint. This defines endWind:π1(Hco,g)→Z after proving the independence and homotopy relations below.
items.locator: Continuation, report topology analysis; journal pp.940–941
api: endWind : FundamentalGroup Hco g →+ Z (using the multiplicative/additive wrapper as needed)
radius_independent : R,R′ beyond a common collar give equal degree
unitTests: endWind(constant loop at g)=0.
endWind(escapingloop)=−1, since its normalized lift is−h(s,r(R)).
endWind(γ*η)=endWind(γ)+endWind(η).

tests.name: endwinding_phase
tests.statement: endWind(escapingloop)=−1, since its normalized lift is−h(s,r(R)).

items.name: End winding is independent of radius and based homotopy
items.statement: For two admissible radii use the radial interval between them and compactchart. For a based homotopy use compactchart with K=I×S1. All normal coordinates remain in C*, so their normalized phases form a homotopy of loops. A common radius for two loops proves additivity by the circle fundamental-group isomorphism.
items.locator: Continuation, report topology analysis; journal pp.940–941

items.name: Infinite-order loop in the compact-open germ space
items.statement: In the Fermat example, endWind([F])=−1; hence endWind is surjective and [F] has infinite order. In particular F does not bound a disk in Hco. A hypothetical disk gives by compactchart a disk in C* with boundary R^(−d)σ(s,r(R))^(−1), whose degree is−1.

items.name: Join of finite nonempty sets has the required connectivity
items.statement: For n≥2 finite nonempty discrete sets A_j of sizes k_j, their join has the homotopy type of a wedge of ∏(k_j−1) spheres S^(n−1), with a zero product meaning a point. Inductively join a CW complex Y with k points, collapse one contractible cone, and obtain k−1 copies of the reduced suspension of Y. Cellular approximation gives (n−2)-connectivity. Generic CW/cofibration and cellular approximation are imported, not replaced by a list of homology ranks.

items.name: Fermat fibre comparison with a finite join
items.statement: For f=Σ_{j=1}^n z_j^k, k≥2, the positive-phase fibre f^−1(R_{>0}) retracts onto the join of n copies of μ_k (Milnor, Lemma9.2). The explicit homeomorphism u↦(f(u)^(−1/k)u,f(u)) identifies it with X×R_{>0}. Thus X is homotopy equivalent to that join; this special homogeneous case does not discharge the general tame-fibre theorem.

items.name: Vanishing of the comparison double-loop fundamental group
items.statement: For the Fermat X and n≥5, finitejoin and fermatjoin give π2(X)=π3(X)=0. Hence Ω²X is path connected and π1(Ω²X)=0, using the pinned loop-space shift at m=0,n=2 and its components equivalence.

items.name: Compact-open interpretation of Lemma7.2 fails in the main range
items.statement: For k=3,d=2,n=40, the nonempty compact-open prescribed-germ space Hco has a fundamental group surjecting onto Z, whereas Ω²X is path connected and simply connected. Consequently Hco is not homotopy equivalent to Ω²X. This refutes the compact-open interpretation, not every topology that could be intended in the unstated source convention.

items.name: A chart with uniform control of the normalized germ
items.statement: Fix a product chart (u,v) near P in Xbar with divisor v=0, a radius ε>0, and a convex tangential ball. For 0<|z|≤ε require u(z)=O(|z|), w(z)=v(z)/z^d=1+O(|z|), u in that ball, and |w−1|<1/2. Equip such tails with the weighted supremum distances of u/|z| and (w−1)/|z|, and combine with the compact-open topology away from the tail. The model includes the fixed radius as data; it is not yet an all-germs topology.

items.name: Fixed-collar extension-space comparison contract
items.statement: For a fixed boundary loop β:S1→X with β(b)=x and a chosen extension to D², let Ext(β) be the compact-open space of extensions. The restriction Map_*(D²,X)→Map_*(S1,X) has the homotopy-lifting property by the CW boundary cofibration and compact-open adjunction; its total space contracts by a disk contraction fixing b. Thus its fibre over β is homotopy equivalent to Ω²X after choosing the reference nullhomotopy. This is a fixed-collar supplier, not an equivalence for Hco.
